column1: # Game profile of Fire Emblem Warriors: Three Hopes (Switch, update v131072 = 1.0.2 over the base game v0, with its DLC stub). Boots on a Retroid Pocket Nova (Turnip T30 and R8); the tutorial and the camp are checked there. Some run-time keys are taken over from Age of Calamity, not measured here
# PEANUTS: a profile this fork added (a Peanuts profile written from a survey of the game files; upstream has none). README.md beside this file
# Koei Tecmo's KTGL engine on NVN, SDK 12.3.7 (Fire Emblem Engage's `sdk` and `subsdk0` builds). Modules main + subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_movie: the WebM movies) + sdk.
# RomFS: the newer RDB (as ROMANCE OF THE THREE KINGDOMS 8 REMAKE): File/CMN/Asset/FDataPackage/Master/root.rdb and system.rdb (indexes, with .rdx) over 1,417 .fdata files (a PDRK header, then
# IDRK entries, LZ4 or zlib chunks) and 28 data/*.file; the movies are loose .webm. LinkData/ holds small LINKDATA .BIN files (no shaders found there)
# The keys below start from Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity (same developer, engine and movie library); none of them is measured on this game
# camera on the right stick (Age of Calamity's; the game's own layout is not checked yet)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk0, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares no system resource (META +0x14 = 0): the game sets its heap with SetHeapSize. The 4 GB block of the other games without virtual address memory, as the survey
# guessed it (the heap check that would measure it does not run on a PC); the same keys as Age of Calamity and Romance of the Three Kingdoms 8 Remake
# no mem_used: the rewritten modules take 59.4 MiB (+ about 2.4 MB of bss), under the default 64 MB by only about 2 MB (Age of Calamity: 66.6 MB, 0x4800000; ROTK8 Remake: 0x5000000).
# If the host log shows SetHeapSize failing against the used memory size, set mem_used to the modules' size rounded up to 2 MB plus 4 MB (about 0x4400000)
# Movie frames (VP9, NV12 to a buffer in a CPU-visible pool, published with nvnMemoryPoolFlushMappedRange), as in Age of Calamity: without the upload its movie stayed black.
# Taken over from it, not seen on this game yet
# KTGL soldiers' Half2 / Short2 attributes feed integer shader inputs, which the replay converts on the CPU: only over the vertices each draw reads (Age of Calamity's
# measurement: millions of vertices a frame in battle otherwise). Taken over from it, not measured here
# PEANUTS: dynamic lights blinking from frame to frame in the camp and in battle: always on, a fix with no player setting (dm/games/README.md tbuf_ssbo_copy; README.md here;
# docs/reference/rendering.md, "Buffer textures over storage buffer stores read a stale copy"). The clustered light-culling compute shader (afe3b29178c63f21) writes the light lists through a
# storage buffer that the pixel shaders read as buffer textures; the host copies those lists on the GPU each frame. Measured on Turnip (T30, R8): one-frame dropouts 14 -> 0 and 4 -> 0, GPU cost
# within 0.4 ms in the camp. Needs placed guest memory, so the system driver keeps the old behaviour. DM_VK_TBUF_GW_SSBO=0 overrides it (developer only)
# PEANUTS: graphics settings by code words in fixed-window mode (shared loader). The game keeps its 1920x1080 window; the 3D size is the float32 ratio of its
# gameplay render-size table (index 2, rodata main+0x1d9f618, 0.75 = 0000403f as the game has it), written from the Output size and DM_SCENE_PCT after the word is checked.
# Output 720p / 1080p / Native (capped at 1080p) sends DM_OUT_SIZE; Internal resolution and Output are Docked only; the composite upscaler rows are hidden
# PEANUTS: Frame rate slider (shared launcher). A words: title needs an fps_limit row; the slider offers 20, 30, 40, 45 and 60 fps (the same steps as the other
# fixed-window titles) and starts at 60 (the game's own rate) with nothing stored. The host frame limiter then runs at the slider's rate (DM_FPS_LIMIT); game speed
# holds at 30 and 40 on the device; 20 and 45 use the same limiter path and are not device-tested
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py: KTGL G2S containers in the .fdata entries, GLSLC outputs in main) ----
